patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg
Secondary_Symptoms: Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders
History of ant bite at the site of the lesion
Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities
Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs

Past_Medical_History: Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on her leg.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“I have a painful ulcerative lesion on my right leg that started as a small red spot about a month ago and has been getting larger. I remember an ant bite at the site before it developed, and now it has a central necrotic base with irregular purplish borders.”
[ASK] Have you had a recent exposure to a toxic chemical or substance (e.g., workplace/household chemicals, fumes, pesticides) before the skin symptoms started?
“No, I don’t recall any chemical or fume exposure or pesticide use before it started. The only thing I can think of is that ant bite right at the spot.”
